title: Canonical manifest origination and automated signing for verified profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: As we scale model onboarding and publish more Redwood-verified performance profiles, we need a single canonical artifact format and an automated signing/origination workflow so consumers (Console, Dedicated, Private agents) can deterministically fetch, verify integrity, and trust the profile metadata used for routing, pinning and cost calculations. Current profile blobs vary by ingestion pipeline (benchmarks service vs manual edits) and there is no standardized canonicalization or signature; that increases risk of mismatch, stale pinning, and manual trust checks.
acceptance_criteria: Define a canonical manifest schema (fields, stable ordering rules, normalization for floating point metrics) and publish spec in Confluence.
Implement a content-addressable canonicalization library in the onboarding service that emits a deterministic SHA256 manifest hash for any profile instance.
Integrate KMS-backed signing: onboarding service will sign canonical manifests using customer-wide KMS key and produce a signed envelope attached to profile artifacts.
Console and runtime clients (hosted API, Dedicated router) can fetch a profile and validate signature/manifest hash; validation failures are logged and trigger fallback routing policy.

Cost normalization: the publishing pipeline normalizes throughput and cost metrics to a common unit (tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-tokens) and records region-anchored variants; documented mapping in the manifesto.
Backwards compatibility: older profiles without signatures remain readable for 90 days with deprecation warnings in Console and onboarding logs.
End-to-end test: benchmark -> manifest -> signed artifact -> client verification run in staging with at least two model examples (decoder-only and encoder-decoder).

2025-01-20 - Andres Vega: Engineering review requested. Key questions: which KMS (AWS KMS vs Vault HSM) and rotation semantics? Also need to confirm manifest size limits and response latency impact on runtime fetch path.

2025-01-22 - Priya Desai (eng): Suggested trade-off: validate signatures async for cached profiles to avoid adding 50-100ms to cold-start path; runtime should verify signature on cache miss synchronously. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/428.

2025-01-27 - Security review (internal notes): signing key will be in central KMS project; rotation policy: automatic re-signing pipeline when key rotates; we must publish key-id and rotation timestamp in the manifest header.

2025-01-30 - Design feedback (Liam Park): Console UX should surface signature status in the profile detail page and show last-verified timestamp; wireframes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1x2-manifest-ui.

2025-02-02 - Andres Vega: Implemented canonicalization lib prototype (python) and unit tests. Benchmarks service updated to emit canonical manifest; sample artifacts in staging bucket s3://redwood-staging/profiles/pm-58219/.

2025-02-04 - Maya Chen: Update: added explicit acceptance criterion for floating point normalization and region anchoring. Next: align with ENG for runtime validation rollout and prepare migration plan for un-signed profiles.
